newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Former HK judge quits race for top 1997 job - paper.
newsitem.headline: Former HK judge quits race for top 1997 job - paper.

text.p: A former Hong Kong High Court judge who said last month he was considering a bid for the territory's leadership after the British leave next year has bowed out of the race, newspapers reported on Saturday.

Arthur Garcia, 71, was quoted by newspapers as saying he was withdrawing because of a lack of support from the community and colleagues in the preparatory committee, which is handling transition matters.
Hong Kong, a British colony for a century and a half, would revert to Chinese rule on July 1, 1997.
Promised a high degree of autonomy, it would be governed by a chief executive chosen in the next two months by a 400-member body selection committee now being formed.

"My deficiency in the Chinese language, particularly in reading, would give me many problems, especially when I had to deal with officials in China," the South China Morning Post reported Garcia, born to a Chinese mother and a Portuguese father, as saying.
Garcia was not immediately available for comment.

His withdrawal leaves four would-be candidates for the top post -- shipping billionaire Tung Chee-hwa, former Chief Justice Sir Ti Liang Yang, lawyer Lo Tak-shing and Hospital Authority chairman Peter Woo.
